did_you_know.text: Did you know? Abijam became king over Judah in the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam son of Nebat, king of Israel.
Did you know? Although Abijam did not wholeheartedly follow the Lord, the Lord preserved the dynasty of David in Jerusalem for David’s sake.
Did you know? Scripture praises David as one who did what was right in the eyes of the Lord and did not turn aside from His commands, but it also mentions his sin involving Uriah the Hittite.
Did you know? Asa reigned in Jerusalem for forty-one years, and his mother’s name was Maacah, daughter of Abishalom.
Did you know? Asa removed his mother Maacah from her position as queen mother because she had made an abominable image for Asherah, and he burned the image in the Kidron Valley.
Did you know? Although the high places were not removed from the land, the Scripture notes that Asa’s heart was fully devoted to the Lord all his days.

Did you know? When Baasha built Ramah to prevent people from entering or leaving Judah, Asa sent silver and gold from the treasuries of the Lord’s temple and the royal palace to Ben-hadad, king of Aram.
Did you know? After Baasha stopped building Ramah, Asa used its stones and timber to build Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah.
Did you know? Baasha son of Ahijah conspired against Nadab son of Jeroboam and killed him at Gibbethon, while Nadab and all Israel were besieging the city.
Did you know? After becoming king, Baasha destroyed the entire house of Jeroboam, fulfilling the word of the Lord spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite.
